PRENATAL DIAGNOSTIC LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Hospital Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Chorionic villi
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Reason for Referral: Advanced maternal age (40 years)
Clinical Indication: Prenatal screening for common trisomies
Gestational Age: 11 weeks 3 days

TEST PERFORMED
Rapid Aneuploidy Detection by Quantitative Fluorescence PCR (QF-PCR)

METHODOLOGY
DNA was extracted from uncultured chorionic villi. Quantitative fluorescence PCR analysis was performed using chromosome-specific short tandem repeat (STR) markers for chromosomes 13, 18 and 21. A minimum of four informative markers were analyzed for each chromosome. The following markers were utilized:

Chromosome 13: D13S631, D13S258, D13S742, D13S628
Chromosome 18: D18S535, D18S391, D18S858, D18S386
Chromosome 21: D21S1435, D21S1411, D21S1412, D21S1446

Peak area ratios were calculated for all informative markers. Normal biallelic ratios range from 0.8-1.4. Ratios outside this range or the presence of three alleles indicate trisomy.

RESULTS

Chromosome 13: Normal diallelic pattern observed
- All markers showed normal biallelic ratios
- No evidence of trisomy 13

Chromosome 18: Normal diallelic pattern observed
- All markers showed normal biallelic ratios
- No evidence of trisomy 18

Chromosome 21: Normal diallelic pattern observed
- All markers showed normal biallelic ratios
- No evidence of trisomy 21

CONCLUSION
Normal complement for chromosomes 13, 18 and 21. No abnormality detected.

INTERPRETATION
This QF-PCR analysis has excluded the common autosomal trisomies (Patau syndrome, Edwards syndrome, and Down syndrome) in this fetal sample. The results indicate a normal chromosomal complement for the three chromosomes tested.

LIMITATIONS
This test is designed to detect whole chromosome aneuploidies of chromosomes 13, 18 and 21 only. It will not detect:
- Balanced chromosomal rearrangements
- Mosaicism below 20%
- Other chromosomal abnormalities
- Single gene disorders
- Maternal cell contamination cannot be excluded without additional testing

RECOMMENDATIONS
Full karyotype analysis of G-banded chromosomes from cultured chorionic villi to follow. This will provide a comprehensive assessment of all chromosomes and detect structural abnormalities not identified by QF-PCR.

Authorized by: [redacted name], PhD, FRCPath
Consultant Clinical Scientist

Report electronically authorized on [redacted date]
